Based on my retrieval in this session (the kb-mcp KB tools are not connected in this environment, so I retrieved from the platform's web-reader tool):

**Answer.** The Transformer computes attention as "Scaled Dot-Product Attention": for each token it derives a Query, Key, and Value vector via learned projections, then computes Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V — dot products of queries with all keys are scaled by √d_k, softmaxed into weights, and used to form a weighted sum of the values (The Annotated Transformer, "Attention" section). The paper uses h = 8 parallel heads with d_k = d_v = d_model/h = 64; each head's output is concatenated and projected by W^O, letting the model attend to different representation subspaces at different positions, with the per-head averaging effect this counteracts. Three uses: encoder self-attention, decoder masked self-attention (future positions set to −∞ before softmax to preserve auto-regressive prediction), and encoder-decoder attention (queries from the decoder, keys/values from the encoder output). Since there is no recurrence or convolution, sinusoidal positional encodings are added to embeddings to inject sequence order. As for why recurrence/convolution are dispensed with: the paper's stated goal is reducing sequential computation — recurrent layers process positions step-by-step, hindering parallelization, while convolutional models (ByteNet, ConvS2S) need operations growing linearly or logarithmically with distance between positions, making long-range dependencies harder to learn; self-attention connects any two positions in a constant number of operations and is far more parallelizable (Abstract + Background, arXiv:1706.03762). Empirically this yielded superior quality at lower training cost: 28.4 BLEU on WMT'14 EN-DE (beating prior best incl. ensembles by >2 BLEU) and 41.8 on EN-FR in 3.5 days on 8 GPUs (Abstract).

**Sources:**
- arXiv:1706.03762 abstract page, "Attention Is All You Need" (Vaswani et al., 2017) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
- The Annotated Transformer (Harvard NLP) — https://nlp.seas.harvard.edu/annotated-transformer/ (sections: Background, Attention, Positional Encoding)
- The Illustrated Transformer (Jay Alammar) — https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-transformer/ (self-attention steps, multi-head, parallelization)
